name: India
genZNote: 28 states, 1 Constitution, 22 scheduled languages, and somehow it all runs on one election machine every five years. India really said 'unity in diversity' and meant it literally.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Seventh-largest country by area, on the Indian subcontinent in South Asia, bordered by Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, and Myanmar, with sea neighbours Sri Lanka and Maldives.
The Himalayas form the northern boundary; the Indo-Gangetic Plain (Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra) dominates the north; the Deccan Plateau covers most of peninsular India.
28 states and 8 Union Territories (following the 2019 Jammu & Kashmir reorganisation into J&K and Ladakh).
Major cities: New Delhi (capital), Mumbai (financial capital), Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: 22 scheduled languages under the Constitution's Eighth Schedule; Hindi and English are the two official languages of the Union government.
Birthplace of four major world religions: Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Sikhism.
40+ UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Taj Mahal, Ajanta & Ellora Caves, and Khajuraho Temples.
Classical dance forms (Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi) and a globally influential film industry centred on Mumbai (Hindi cinema).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic under a parliamentary system, per the Constitution of India (adopted 26 Nov 1949, in force 26 Jan 1950).
Bicameral Parliament: Lok Sabha (directly elected lower house) and Rajya Sabha (upper house, representing states).
President is the constitutional head of state; the Prime Minister, backed by the Lok Sabha majority, heads the government.
World's largest democracy by population, holding the largest-scale general elections on Earth.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Home to ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) — notable for Chandrayaan-3's south-pole Moon landing (2023) and a cost-efficient space programme.
One of the world's largest producers of generic medicines, often called the 'pharmacy of the world'.
Extensive public vaccination infrastructure, notably scaled up during the COVID-19 pandemic (Covishield/Covaxin manufacturing).
Major IT and software services hub, with Bengaluru and Hyderabad as leading technology centres.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement; a member of the United Nations, G20, BRICS, SAARC, and the Commonwealth of Nations.
A Quad (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue) member alongside the United States, Japan, and Australia.
Regularly participates in international climate commitments, including a 2030 non-fossil-fuel energy capacity target announced around COP26.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: One of the world's largest and fastest-growing major economies by GDP, with services, IT, agriculture, and manufacturing as core sectors.
Major exports: petroleum products, pharmaceuticals, IT services, textiles, gems and jewellery, engineering goods.
The 'Make in India' initiative and the India Semiconductor Mission are recent efforts to expand domestic manufacturing, including chip assembly and fabrication.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: The Taj Mahal, Himalayan mountaineering, Bollywood, yoga, spices, and a globally influential IT services industry.
ISRO's cost-efficient space missions; being the world's most populous country and largest democracy.

sections.heading: 📰 Current Affairs Connection (2026)
sections.body: For up-to-date, curated 2026 developments involving India — the Union Budget 2026-27, ISRO missions, NEET updates, and more — see Cellfie's Current Affairs 2026 module, which is kept as its own dated, sourced section rather than duplicated here.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Indian Rupee (₹, INR), issued and regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank founded in 1935.
One of the world's largest and fastest-growing major economies, with services (especially IT), agriculture, and manufacturing as the three broad pillars.

Major industries: information technology and software services, textiles, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, steel, and agriculture (India is among the largest producers of milk, rice, wheat, and sugarcane).
Natural resources include coal, iron ore, and a large arable land base that supports its agricultural sector.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Home to four global biodiversity hotspots: the Himalayas, the Western Ghats, the Indo-Burma region, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).
The Sundarbans (shared with Bangladesh) is the world's largest mangrove forest and a Bengal tiger habitat, protected under Project Tiger (started 1973).

Major ecosystems range from Himalayan alpine zones and the Thar Desert to tropical rainforests in the Western Ghats and Northeast, plus extensive coastal and marine ecosystems along its ~7,500 km coastline.
Faces environmental challenges including air pollution in major cities, water stress, and glacial retreat in the Himalayas, alongside growing renewable-energy and afforestation efforts.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Ancient period: one of the world's oldest continuous civilizations, tracing back to the Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2500 BCE) and later Vedic, Mauryan, and Gupta empires.
Colonial period: came under British Crown rule in 1858 (after over a century of East India Company control), following the 1857 revolt.
Independence: gained independence from British rule on 15 August 1947, alongside the Partition that created Pakistan.
Republic: became a sovereign republic when its Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, now celebrated annually as Republic Day.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1950: Constitution of India comes into force, establishing a sovereign democratic republic.
1956: States Reorganisation Act redraws internal state boundaries largely along linguistic lines.
1991: Landmark economic liberalisation reforms open India's economy to global trade and investment.
2019: Jammu and Kashmir is reorganised into two Union Territories (Jammu & Kashmir, and Ladakh), following the reading down of Article 370's special provisions.
2017: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) reform unifies most indirect taxes into a single nationwide tax system.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), founded in 1969, runs one of the world's most cost-efficient space programmes.
Chandrayaan-3 (2023) made India the first country to land near the Moon's south pole and the fourth to achieve a soft lunar landing overall.
Aditya-L1 (launched 2023) is India's first dedicated solar observation mission, studying the Sun from the Sun-Earth L1 point.
The Digital India and India Stack initiatives (including the Aadhaar digital identity system and UPI real-time payments) have driven large-scale digital public infrastructure.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Cricket is the most widely followed sport; India has won the Cricket World Cup multiple times and hosts the globally popular Indian Premier League (IPL).
Chess has seen a recent surge, with Indian players including a teenage World Chess Champion (2024) reflecting a broader boom in the sport.
Mumbai's Hindi film industry ('Bollywood') is one of the world's largest film industries by number of films produced annually.
40+ UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Taj Mahal, and classical arts such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, and Hindustani/Carnatic classical music, recognised internationally.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of the United Nations (1945) and the Non-Aligned Movement.
Member of the G20, BRICS, SAARC, the Commonwealth of Nations, and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).
A Quad (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue) member alongside the United States, Japan, and Australia.
Active participant in WHO, UNESCO, WTO, and the World Bank/IMF, and a long-standing contributor to UN peacekeeping missions.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: India is a parliamentary democratic republic in South Asia, the world's most populous country and largest democracy, with 28 states and 8 Union Territories.
keyFacts: Capital: New Delhi. Currency: Indian Rupee (₹). Constitution in force: 26 January 1950.
22 scheduled languages; Hindi and English are the two official Union languages.
Founding member of NAM; member of G20, BRICS, SAARC, Commonwealth, and the Quad.
commonConfusion: India's Constitution was ADOPTED on 26 November 1949 but came INTO FORCE on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day) — two different dates.

highYieldFacts: Constitution: adopted 26 Nov 1949, in force 26 Jan 1950.
22 scheduled languages under the Eighth Schedule.
commonTraps: Confusing India's independence date (15 Aug 1947) with the Constitution's commencement date (26 Jan 1950).
Assuming Hindi is India's sole official language — English shares official status at the Union level.
mustRemember: India: parliamentary democratic republic, bicameral Parliament (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha), President as head of state.
